newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to limit sunflower exports-Ag Minister.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to limit sunflower exports-Ag Minister.

text.p: Ukraine intends to limit sunflower exports so it can boost domestic oil and margarine production, deputy prime minister of agriculture Mykhailo Zubets said on Friday.
"There is a problem with sunflowers. We have 18 refineries which are privatised, but which are not working," Zubets told a conference of private agriculture businesses.
"That is because they have no raw supplies to work with. The 1.2 million tonnes of sunflower produced last year went beyond our borders," Zubets said.
Ukraine produced 2.3 million tonnes of sunflowers last year compared to 2.9 million tonnes in 1995.
Its refineries produced 572,800 tonnes of sunflower oil and exported about 320,000 tonnes of sunflower seed to European countries and Turkey last year, the Statistics Ministry said.

"We must unite the refineries into a company or league, give them investment credits, support them and make agreements with producers to make branch work again," Zubets said, promising to implement the plan soon.
Zubets, who also promised to bring grain production to 50 million tonnes a year in several years, has been criticised by Western experts for employing Soviet methods in running the sector.
Last year Ukraine produced a record-low grain crop of 25.4 million tonnes, half the 50-million-tonne harvests produced prior to independence in 1991.
